...trying hard not to look at you. When she withdrew and you held on to her hand she tried not to look at your face and see the expression there.
A long sigh, one millennia in the making.
Dolores Dei -- the innocence of humanism, internationalism, and the welfare state -- turns around to face you. She has an airship bag in her hand. She seems to be in a hurry.
Her chest rising like a pillow, warm exhalations against the side of your mouth -- her tender soul moving through her lungs.
Her hand does not return the grip. Her body is rigid. A current of unease courses through it.
Her innocence Dolores Dei fiddles with the handle of her airport bag. She has a *pained* expression on her face. It's agonizing.
It does not. It goes on. Children run in the back alleys. Pigeons take flight. She shakes her head one more time as the evening wind rustles her hair.
No answer. The arches of her brows quiver as she looks you in the eye and backs away from you...
Nothing, just pillows against you. Unresponsive... but for the taste of apricots.
She breathes out, heavily, as if something painful has passed through her -- and shakes her head.
She breathes out, impatiently.
She does not answer. There's that expression again.
She does not look back, instead eyes her fingernails. They're bitten, frayed. The evening wind blows in, the gown wraps around her like a white flag.
She does not seem relieved at all. Glances over her shoulder, then at you... the neon sign of the video rental glows behind her...
She doesn't know what to say.
She doesn't reply. You're back in your head. There's silence.
She doesn't say anything. It’s excruciating.
She doesn’t say anything. It’s excruciating.
She is not kissing you back.
She keeps glancing over her shoulder nervously. "I haven't even bought the tickets yet..."

She looks at her toenails sticking out from under the gown. "Everyone has a little glass of wine every now and then. I certainly do. It's a *queen regnant* thing. I don't think it was the alcohol -- it was *inevitability*."
She looks at the Headless FALN Rider between your fingers and doesn't know what to say.
She looks at the suitcase, not knowing what more to say, then over her shoulder.
She shakes her head one more time. The evening wind rustles her hair, blowing old newspapers and fast food wrappings down the street...
She shakes her head. "I am actually very ordinary, Harry. Below this gown and wreath I have an ordinary soul and ordinary thoughts. The only thing inhuman about me is this..." She looks around.
She shakes her head. "Let's stop it with the apes, this isn't going anywhere."
She sighs and looks over her shoulder.
She sighs in frustration. "Then why are you *doing* this?"
She sighs with frustration: "My friends are waiting for me on the platform. I can't let them wait -- it's impolite."
She smiles mysteriously, looking east. Then turns her gaze back to you. The smile is gone.
She tried not to look at you -- when she withdrew and you held on to your hand. She tried not to look at your face and see the expression there.
The advisor to the queen of Suresne sighs and looks down -- at the crumbling asphalt. There is nothing she can do about your chest pain.
The air gets cold around you. She looks down on her stomach, then up at you. Her eyes are full of tremendous distance and mystery.
The delicate wreath on her forehead, pressing into your temple. The silver is cold from the spring evening air.
The gown moves on her limbs, like water. She breathes out, her breath heavy. You're running out of ideas.
The light from the video rental casts shadows on the ground. She turns her face and it's illuminated by it. Red and cyan...
The moment is ending. She is going to move her face away from yours...
The mysterious smile on her lips keeps stretching wider, as if she's forgotten you're there. In some great and calming thought. Then she notices you -- and it's immediately gone.
There is a silence. She looks at you, then over her shoulder. Then corrects the wreath on the dome of her forehead.
They're turning moist now, her eyes. She slowly shakes her head and tries to get a hold of herself, brushing her hands in her gown...
Where? There's water all around. She turns her face and it's illuminated by the sign of the video rental... Red and cyan...
"*Why* did you do that to yourself? You know I don't cheat, Harry. I never cheated on you."
"... but now, only boring hell remains." Her crown-of-hair is aglow with the red of the neon on the corner. Like this, she tramples her feet for warmth. It's getting *really* cold outside.

"... it was *a hundred million years ago*. I was someone else then -- filled to the brim with love for you. Hanging on your every word. Oh Harry, you were the *coolest*... But I am no longer that person. This..." She points to herself. "... has taken her place. It will devour you. Harry -- I will eat your mind."
"A cop... You've worked there for so long you can't even talk like a normal person anymore! It's always lists with you. *Questions*."
"A little down? You've worked there for so long you can't even talk like a normal person anymore! It's always lists with you. *Questions*."

"A street called Voyager Road." She smiles, sadly. "It was a million years ago, Harry. No -- it was a *hundred million* years ago. We were so, so young then. I loved you more than you will ever know. I loved you more than anyone has ever loved *anyone*."
"An immortal temple of light? That sounds nice. I *do* want someone to do that for me -- who wouldn't? -- but not you. I don't want *anything* from you."

"And my Crown of Immortality? No." She shakes her head. "You scared her out of me. With your crying, your..." She stops. "The awful time we wound up having. In the cheap rental flats you could afford..."
"Anyway."
"As *queen regnant* I write a lot of letters." She brushes a strand of white hair out her eye.
"At first, yes. I *was* angry at you. But I truly am *not* anymore. My life is in a very good place..." She glances over her shoulder.
"Besides, you're only saying this because things didn't work out between us." She stops. "I really have to go to the aerodrome, I don't have time for this."
"But -- I can."

"But Harry, it doesn’t look like you rebuilt yourself, it looks like you fell apart without me. I can’t bare to look at it any more, okay? I feel *guilty*. That’s what I feel when I look at you. Please let me go..."

"But it is gone now. Nothing came of it. No children, nothing built. We live in the coldest of all possible worlds, Harry, orbiting the most distant star. It is agony, sheer agony..." She shakes her head slowly: "How *bad* I have to go to the aerodrome."
"Call me like that..."
"Can't you see -- I can never think you're cool again. I can only think that way about *new* people."

"Do you know how much it hurts me to hear you say that?" She sounds downright angry. "I'm shit, you made me shit... I can't do this any more. I can't make you *insane* and *shit* any more, I can't let you turn me into a bad person. I have to go..."
"Don't say that... I know this *positive* thing sounds stupid to you, Harry, but it works. We all have an obligation to be happy. You too. And you *will* be. Now..." She looks over her shoulder...
"Don't think like that, Harry..." She smiles.
"Exactly, now..." She glances over her shoulder. You hear distant traffic. An airship passes overhead, dogs bark somewhere.
"Forty-two," she nods sadly. "That is the light rail that took me to Couron, to school and work. Every morning... it's the same stop I met you at, Harry. A hundred thousand million years ago..."
"God, Harry..." She shakes her head, her eyebrows knitting together with worry.
"Good. That’s... very nice." She doesn’t sound appropriately impressed.
"Great," she nods. "It's the abyss of the void. Soon it will be 'the gloaming'; then it will be the 'world-ending'... My friends are waiting for me on the platform, Harry. It's impolite to..."
"Great. Now I'm the *symbol of pain*." The smile immediately disappears from her face. The air remains just as cold.
"Harry, I don't want things. I want to go to the aerodrome."
"Harry, do you notice how... none of this is very *funny*?"

"Harry, it doesn’t look like you’re *hard* at all, it looks like you fell apart without me. I can’t bare to look at it any more, okay? I feel *guilty*. That’s what I feel when I look at you. Please let me go..."
"Harry, we can't be together because you're insane." Her eyes turn to sorrowful ovals.
"Hey."
"I *have* to, Harry. Really, I've already missed the 8:30..." Her fingers wrap around the bag handle. "I'm gonna go now..."

"I am impolite with you, Harry, because you are the past. Me and those friends will have good times, together, in the future..." The evening wind blows in, the gown wraps around her like a white flag. She says:
"I can't answer your *other questions*, Harry. Not anymore... I have to go."
"I can't do that anymore. I'm not eighty years old, I'm thirty two. People my age are not supposed to mourn..." She breathes out, it sounds more angry than a sigh.
"I can’t do this talk again..." She sounds like she’s going to cry -- but not in a good way.
"I didn't *ask* for things. It's too late to give me anything. I would have liked the Headless FALN Rider -- back then..."
"I didn't *ask* for things. It's too late to give me anything. I would have liked these things, a long time ago -- the Headless FALN Rider especially..."
"I didn't ask for them either. They're just a folk tale that has nothing to do with my reign, or the direction I have set our species on..." She glances over her shoulder, then back at you.
"I don't know what that *means*..." She sighs with frustration. "My friends are waiting for me on the platform. I can't let them wait -- it's impolite."
"I don't know what you mean, Dolores Dei?" She looks at you quizzically. It does not seem like a mystery she wants to get into.
"I don't know why I said *but*. There is no but."
"I don't know. Please..." She shuffles from one golden-sandaled foot to the other. In the distance a street car screeches.
"I don't want it..." She doesn't take it. "It looks expensive. I don't want it."
"I don’t... I don’t know what to say. I’m tired."
"I hate being that. I don't want to be anything for you. I hope the decades it takes for you to get over me have already passed."
"I have to go there even more than I used to love you. And *that's* saying something." She looks at her travel bag.
"I have to wipe it all off me -- and be clean again. I want to be a good person again, not this. Not what you made me into."
"I mean -- hey to you too?" she says apprehensively.
"I really, really, *really* have to go there. No human being in the history of the world has ever had to go to the *aerodrome* as much as I have to go there now. You see, Harry..."
"I terminated yours. Don't you remember, you *poor* fuck? Poverty-stricken fuck."
"I terminated yours. Don't you remember, you *poor* fuck? You poverty-stricken fuck."
"I told you -- good things can still happen."
"I will," she says. The evening wind blows in and the gown wraps around her like a white flag.
"I won't see you but you will see me."
"I'm doing really good, actually. Both professionally and romantically. I've come to a fulfilling and peaceful period in my life." She nods hastily. "How are you doing, Harry?"
"I'm glad too, but I have to go. My friends are waiting for me on the platform. I can't let them wait -- it's impolite."
"I'm going to Mirova. To live there -- in Graad. It's one million kilometres away, Harry. Might as well be another lifetime."

"I'm not a star. I'm a confused young woman, eating your mind. There are no stars. There is no light. There will be no future. There is only this intersection. And the aerodrome. Where I must go, incessantly, brutally -- utterly without redemption or hope."
"I'm not that either... Can't I just *be*?"
"I'm pregnant."
"I'm sorry. I was heading to the aerodrome, I just don't have time to..." She stops mid sentence, glances to her right. Then looks at her bag.
"I'm suffocatingly beautiful. And young. And I smell of tutti frutti chewing gum -- like I did that time when I asked you for forgiveness. After leaving you the first time, so long ago..."
"In conclusion -- you're ill. You're an old, insane man. And you have to be in hell until the end of your life. And I have to go to Mirova."
"In the aerodrome there are silver-rotored ships, and beautiful flying trains I will go away on. It's a nice, peaceful place."

"Is there really anything left? If not, we can always repeat one of the things we have already talked about. Talk about it *again*..." She looks over her shoulder. "If you do not to feel like doing that, you should let me go the aerodrome."
"It doesn't look like it did, Harry. I'm sorry. I shouldn't have wrote you any letters. I was too young then..."

"It doesn’t sound like you're better at all, Harry. It doesn’t even sound like you're a moralist, it just sounds like you want to..." She spreads her arms. "*Win me back* or something. I don't want you to try that any more, okay? It's too sad, I need to *go*..."
"It is -- and it's making me late for my beautiful-beautiful flight to Mirova. Far, far away from you -- and Revachol."
"It is. Useless..." The evening wind blows in as she says the words, her gown wraps around her like a white flag.

"It just takes some time. For you, I think it will take something like... twenty years maybe? It was hard for me too, you know -- I used to think I couldn't live without you..." She looks you straight in the eye -- her irises are light blue, flecked with green.

"It was a hundred million years ago, Harry... No, make it a thousand million years ago. Practically on another planet." She looks at her travel bag, thoughtfully: "Have I told you how bad I need to go to the aerodrome?"

"It was just a day then, but to think! Were we there now, you could touch my hair, kiss me. Talk to me about anything; go..." She shakes her head. "...virtually *anywhere* in the world. Not like now -- now our interactions are limited to *pain and regret*."
"It wasn't a fight. I was never fighting you."
"It will pass..." The gown moves on her limbs, like water. "Everything does."
"It's all gone. I have to go to the aerodrome. I have to leave Revachol and you. And you have to be alone -- in hell, forever. That's just the way it is."
"It's here, Harry." She looks around. "We are *on* Voyager Road. At the end of it -- three hundred metres from the stop. We used to come here to rent videos."
"It's here." She looks around. "We are *on* Voyager Road. At the end of it -- three hundred metres from the stop. We used to come here to rent videos."
"It's not about some tie, Harry! You've worked there for so long you can't even talk like a normal person anymore! It's always lists with you. *Questions*."

"It's not just the lists, or trees, or whatever..." She corrects the wreath on her head, with her hands trembling now. "You get sad, Harry. *Too* sad. People can't get that sad. It's impossible to watch..."
"It's not just the lists..." She corrects the wreath on her head, with her hands trembling now. "You get sad, Harry. *Too* sad. People can't get that sad. It's impossible to watch..."
"It's not, but..." She looks at her feet. Little golden sandals cover her toes.
"It's okay." She puts no effort into making it sound as if it's actually okay.
"It's okay."
"It’s about taking care of yourself. Life is not a competition."
"It’s not about *paper*, Harry, or anything like that..." She sounds frustrated.

"I’m so tired, Harry. I’m so tired of all this..." She sighs. "Can’t you see, I already *am* trapped in amber with you? We’re stuck here. I can’t do that any more. The aerodrome is the future. It is laughter and ease... I must go."
"Just my scepter, my *globe crucigère*, a spare silk gown. A toothbrush. Travel documents. The Crown of Immortality."
"Light, life, *culture*... It's so much better than here. Everything here reminds me of you, and the horrible times we had. The nights we stayed up fighting for our dying love."
"Months already. Soon it will be years without the hurt. I sit there in Mirova -- in the holy gratitude of my bliss -- I put my hand on my belly and *smile...*
"Months already. Soon it will be years. Every season that passes the lights get less clear. I sit there, in Mirova -- in the holy gratitude of my bliss -- I put my hand on my belly and *smile...*"
"My lungs do not *glow*, Harry. I am just like all the others. None of us have glowing lungs -- stop making me into some kind of..."
"No human being should still remember the position of atoms such... aeons ago. It must feel unnaturally sad -- a sadness so ancient, it is shared even by archaebacteria."
"No, Harry, we can't."
"No, Harry. No human being in the history of the world has ever had to go to the *aerodrome* as much as I have to go there now. You see..."
"No, Harry. Not yet. There is one more thing you have to see..." She slides her hands down her chest, and onto her lower stomach. And smiles.

"No, Harry." She shakes her head sadly. "No. I don't want a *massive, epic showdown*. I want to go to the aerodrome. I have tickets for the 10:20 flight to Mirova..." She looks at you plaintively. "Really..."
"No, Harry." She shakes her head. "It's just regular skin. I'm not as beautiful as you always thought I was. Let's not get into..."
"No, Harry." She shakes her head.

"No, it's all you. I always loved you for it -- but it could not save us. It could not make me stay. In the end your mind just told you precisely how *bad* things are, and who would want to stay around for that?"
"No, it’s not... I’m glad you’re finally taking care of yourself financially. I really am, but you need to do it for yourself. Not me. I don’t need it. I need to *run-run-run* to the aerodrome!"
"No, you *don't*. You've worked there for so long you can't even talk like a normal person anymore! It's always lists with you. *Questions*."
"No, you don't. You're just being a martyr. And I'm really going now. The time is up. I must be on the 10:20 flight..." She turns.
"No. It's too late. I found someone for whom I feel the same love I did for you. Only this time -- he is more careful, he will not lose me. It will go somewhere. It will grow..."
"No. Please. Please don't give me anything."
"No. That would only be painful and dull. At the aerodrome -- life, love, and laughter are waiting for me. At the cafeteria -- dust, hell, and tragicomedy."
"No. Too late now. You have forgotten your list and the time is up. I am really going now. I must be on the 10:20 flight..." She turns.
"No. You scared it out of me. With your crying. Your hysteric..." She stops. "The awful time we wound up having. In the cheap rental flats you could afford..."
"No..." She just shakes her head once more. "I'm just Dora."

"Not married. We were *engaged* then, living in a little house on the outskirts of Central Jamrock, past the lake that formed when a mainline pipe burst in the early Twenties. At the end of a street called..."
"Nothing -- I have to go..." Her hand wraps around the handle of the bag in her hand again: "I'm gonna go now..."
"Now, go ahead..." She wipes her palms into the silk of her gown. "...ask me more questions. Let's talk about *something else*."
"Of course not." She looks down at her belly, then up into your old eyes...
"Of course, you're a visionary entrepreneur, and I'm a *social democrat* -- because I don't want to keep hurting you..." She looks away from you.
"Oh my god, Harry! Stop. I don't want to hear anything about *the mourning*, mourning someone who's still alive -- *any of that*!"
"Oh no, no-no-no-no." She shakes her head. "We're not doing that again."
"Oh, Harry, this is a dream, can't you see? I'm already in Mirova by now. Who knows how long ago this happened?" She looks around. "A year, two, *five* years ago?"
"Oh, Harry. You shouldn't have done that..." She shakes her head very slowly, her white hair brushing her shoulders.
"Oh, Harry... I don't need you to forgive. It's a *good* thing for me." She smiles. "It's good news, why aren't you smiling more?"
"Oh, Harry... There is only one way for humans to last forever -- and you did not do that to me..." She shakes her head.

"Oh, Harry? Do you really think so? We haven't talked in *years*... I don't want to call you. I don't want to hear from you. I think of you less and less every year, weeks go by without me remembering you..."
"Oh, this?" She corrects the wreath on her forehead.
"Oh, yes. This is real darkness. It's not death, or war, or child molestation. Real darkness has love for a face. The first death is in the heart, Harry."

"Okay, Harry." She sighs. "Okay. It was morning and you slept. The room smelled of cigarettes and rowans. There was hoarfrost on the ground, when I left. It was autumn, the first one we had together. But you have to understand -- it was a million years ago. No..."
"Okay, stop. Yes," she surrenders. "Are you happy now?"
"Other people get sad too, but not like you, you stay down for too long -- and if you're not down, you're up, running around asking questions. Millions of questions..."
"Other people get sad too, but not like you, you stay down for too long. Until you start giving your thoughts *names* and talking to things..."
"Other people get sad too, but not like you, you stay down for too long. You only communicated with *encyclopaedic trivia*... I was so alone."
"Other people get sad too, but not like you. You stay down for years, and then you start beating things... You get violent."
"Other questions are the last thing I need right now..." She cups her ear.  "Hush, can you hear? I think that's the 42..."
"Please don't give me any gifts..." She looks at the airport bag, then at you.
"Please, Harry, I just don't have time for this."
"Please, Harry..." The gown moves on her limbs, like water. "I don't understand what you're saying. You're pitiful and frightening, a smoky apparition of its former self."

"Right here. Tomorrow night. Once this dream starts happening it keeps happening -- three times a week. At least. And Harry, it really, really looks like it's started *happening* again. There's the video rental..."
"See you tomorrow."
"See? *Let's talk about something else*..." She sighs.

"See?" Her eyes widen. "It just takes some time. For you, I think it will take something like... twenty years maybe? It was hard for me too. I used to think I couldn't *live* without you..." She looks you straight in the eye -- her irises are light blue, flecked with green.

"See?" She smiles -- as if a weight is lifted off her shoulders.
"Sometimes. You can be very safe, but..." They're turning moist now. She slowly shakes her head and tries to get a hold of herself, brushing her hands in her gown...

"Sometimes... Not as often as I used to. So much time has passed. More than it seems here..." She stares at her feet -- the zebra stripes on the intersection. The lights of the video rental glow in her hair.
"Stop laughing like that, please. It's *scary*."
"That is *very* contested by modern historians." She tramples her little feet for warmth and adds: "Very contested. Plus..."

"That sounds like it would be in the news... I don't want that, okay?" There's a pause. "Please don't name it that. You discovering a new species changes nothing. If someone else discovered a new species and named it after me, then I would be flattered. But not you."
"That sounds nice, Harry, but I really don't want to argue about *ideology* with you right now..."
"That was someone else. I betrayed her, overwrote her, and am happier for it. And I'm really going now. The time is up -- I must be on the 10:20 flight..." She turns.
"That's it, yes," she looks up from her toes. "We've talked about it a million times. You will get over it, just like I did. People do. Things will get good for you again..."
"That's not what the figurines do, Harry."

"The coolest..." She closes her eyes: "With your leather jacket and your boot cut pants. Smoking in the bus stop. I wanted you to be the rest of my life that day. And you were -- some of it, at least. You were my first. My first kiss, my first time to have sex."
"The first -- and worst -- time I fell in love. I will always have that with me. It's a fact. But that is all it is. It's like a ticket stub, Harry. It doesn't *do* anything anymore."
"The morning? I don't understand."
"The poetry thing is not going to help. It's only going to make things worse. I *really* have to go... I don't even know how you got here."
"The questions will not bring those times back, Harry." She shakes her head slowly.
"Then why are we doing it?" The advisor to the queen of Suresne sighs and looks down -- at the crumbling asphalt.
"Then why are we doing this?" The advisor to the queen of Suresne sighs and looks down -- at the crumbling asphalt.
"There is nothing else."

"There was a time I would have loved to hear about them. I would have hung on every word. I would have made you feel smart, just, hopeful. But now is not that time. Now we are in hell and in hell there is only the aerodrome. And boring disagreement."

"There." She points across the water, into the darkness. "You could not pay the electrical bill. It became a lightless tomb. The years you spent training for the militia, my parents' money... It was not good."

"They shouldn't have. They really shouldn't. I was in Mirova already. Safe. In the warmth of the night. Wrapped in my future love. There, I think of you less and less, whole weeks go by without me remembering you..."
"This *thing* you've made me into. I'm sorry for saying so, but I just *hate* it. What is this? This is so far gone, Harry, I don't even..."
"This is another list, isn't it?"
"This is another one, isn't it? We're in a *tree* right now!"
"This is how human beings operate."
"This is just a wreath. The Crown of Immortality is made of rarefied light, manna, and raw palladium. It was passed on to me by the rulers of late antiquity..."

"Very well," she sighs. "I wrote it. It was morning, you slept. There was hoarfrost on the ground when I left. On Voyager Road. It was autumn, the first autumn. But Harry, please understand -- it was a million years ago. No..."

"Voyager Road 21A." She nods sadly. "It was so long ago. It was a million years ago, Harry. No -- a hundred million years ago. I loved you more than you will ever know. I loved you more than anyone has ever loved *anyone*."
"Wasn't I Dolores Dei just a second ago? Now I'm the *ex-thing*... You're confusing me. Look, I have to be at the Lausanne Aerodrome at 10:20 PM. I still have a light rail to catch..."
"We already tried again and it didn't work."
"We both said a lot of things. We were very young."
"We don't have anything to talk about anymore. Every combination of words has been played out. The atoms don't form us anymore: us, our love, our unborn daughters..."
"We were bad for each other, okay? I was bad for you. Can you not see, I'm *bad*? I had to stop, I couldn't just turn into a bad person... You *will* get better."
"We will always have what was." She leans on her hand luggage and smiles faintly: "I will always be *influenced* by it. But it is over. Now only total, unrelenting hell remains."
"Well, I'm in my head too. We're all in our heads."
"What *other things*?" She shakes her head. "We've been through *all* the things, Harry..."
"What do you mean stopped saying things?"
"Who says that? I have ruled with kindness, grace and temperance. It's perfectly normal to have an Army of Humanity. I am the innocence of humanism -- I call it whatever I want to."
"Why what?"
"Wow -- see? A new species..." She smiles. It's another sad smile, with knitted brows.
"Wow, see? The entire case..." She smiles. It's another sad smile, with knitted brows.
"Yes, Harry, it's me." She sighs.

"Yes, Harry. I am. Things have gotten *much* better for me -- now that I am the ruler of the known world..." She pulls up the silvery sleeve of her gown, to check the time. "Oh god, it's already so late, I have to *go*, Harry."
"Yes. But that time is gone now. So *very* gone."
"Yes. He did it." She looks down at her belly, then up into your old eyes...
"Yes. I have found someone. For whom I can feel the same -- a copy of my love for you, only this time he is careful and rich. He will not lose me. It will go somewhere. It will grow..."
"Yes. It only took me one year, maybe two." She smiles and wipes her brow in relief: "Whooh."
"Yes. It really, *really* is better that I don't."

"Yes. Let's talk about that too." She nods. "Let's bring it up -- the zoo. In Le Jardin. The day we went east of the river. To the aquarium first... I was sad about my mother. I don't even know why. The shimmer of the fish tank on my face, the octopuses..."
"Yes. Of course. I'm *bourgeois* -- because I don't want to keep hurting you..." She looks away from you.
"Yes. Of course. You're a kingsman and I'm a socialist traitor, because I don't want to keep hurting you..." She looks away from you.
"Yes. Of course. You've got everything under control and I'm hysterical because I don't want to keep hurting you..." She looks away from you.
"Yes. Okay. I'm glad."
"Yes." She looks over her shoulder again. "I mean no. But I *am* in a hurry."
"Yes."

"You don't have to hate the world." She looks around her, at the evening light. "Can't you see how kind and beautiful everything is? I don't have time to deal with your pessimism -- there are so many people at the stop at this hour. They're all going to the aerodrome."
"You have to take care of yourself. You're not a young man anymore. If you keep going like this you'll..." She falls silent.
"You know what I mean..."
"You know what I meant. We're talking about it again. It came up again. This conversation is about *that* again."
"You know what this means."
"You were very bad to me too..." She stops. "We've talked about it like seven million times now, I don't want to do that anymore."
"You're only saying this because things didn't work out between us. I have to go to the aerodrome now. I don't have time to defend myself from these accusations."
"You're right. I *was* angry at you. But I truly am *not* anymore. My life is in a very good place..." She glances over her shoulder.
"You're yelling, Harry." She stops. "I can't do this. I can't be *afraid* of your emotions anymore. I can't talk about *mad paper* or any of it. Please just let me go."
